## Class

**47 `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests. Mock the network call (e.g.
unittest.mock.patch('urllib…'))`** in job `100874330553` — the second-largest class after S1 and
the largest of the non-`lock.py` remainder.

The guard is doing its job in the sense that it fires; the defect is that on Windows it fires for
call paths that on POSIX are already mocked or never taken. Either the guard's interception point
differs by platform (a different socket/`urllib` entry point is reached), or a fixture that
installs the mock is itself skipped or failing on Windows and the guard is the *symptom* of that.

Determine which before changing the guard. A guard that is loosened to make Windows quiet would
delete the very protection the 47 firings prove is working.

## Blocked by S1

These tests may be firing the guard only because a preceding store write failed and pushed the test
down an unmocked fallback path. Re-measure after S1 lands; the class size is an upper bound.

## Proving command

```
uv run --no-sync pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1 \
  | grep -c "Network access is forbidden"   # must be 0
```
on `windows-latest`, and the same command on `ubuntu-latest` must also report 0 — proving the guard
was not weakened to reach the Windows number.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Zero `Network access is forbidden` RuntimeErrors in a Windows sweep.
2. The guard still fires on a deliberately unmocked call, proven by a test that asserts the guard
   raises — the fix must not be "disable the guard on Windows".
